title: Mother's Name
next_chapter_hook: The jade pendant that had been quietly glowing among the ruins seemed to sense Chen Ji's presence, trembling gently—as if calling out a name that had vanished for fifteen years.

text.content: In the instant of blood resonance, Chen Ji felt as if his chest had been pierced by thunder and fire—a surge of warmth erupted from the depths of his heart, piercing through bone marrow and rushing to his brow center. The familiar sensation that made his heart race echoed the gentle touch of his mother's cool palm on his forehead during childhood fevers, the quiet rhythm of her hand patting his back on countless nights of nightmares. Fifteen years had passed, and he believed he had long forgotten such feelings.

Chen Ji abruptly pressed his hand against his chest, his knuckles turning white. He could sense that connection—not one-directional, but like the relationship between a kite and its string. He pulled gently from this end, and his sister would respond softly from the other. The threads of destiny became unprecedentedly clear at this moment, as if he could follow this bloodline to find her simply by wanting to.

But he didn't act immediately. Years of scheming had cultivated in him the habit of remaining calm in any situation, even as his heart raced wildly in his chest and his fingertips trembled. He took a deep breath, suppressing the surging emotions, and began to survey his surroundings. That place where the aura had erupted was just beyond the rock wall, some thirty feet away.

There was a crack in the rock wall, from which faint light filtered through. Chen Ji activated his spiritual energy to protect his body, then squeezed through sideways. At the end of the narrow passage was a small sealed chamber, untouched for countless years. When he clearly saw the chamber's contents, his footsteps came to an abrupt halt.

In the center of the chamber on a stone platform stood a portrait. In the painting, two people stood shoulder to shoulder—the man in blue robes, with clear and handsome features, was clearly Chen Xuan in his youth. And the woman... Chen Ji's breath stopped at that moment. She had eyebrows and eyes exactly as he remembered, the faint red tear mole at the corner of her eye, and that barely perceptible smile at the corner of her lips—it was his mother.

dialogue.content: (The residual soul's voice echoed幽幽) You have finally found this place. It seems the guidance of fate has never strayed from its course.

text.content: Chen Ji did not turn around; he only stared at that familiar yet strange figure in the portrait. Fifteen years—he had tried to recall his mother's appearance and voice, yet found he couldn't even remember her voice clearly. That woman who quietly left when he was seven, who last touched his head before leaving and said 'Wait for me to come back'—who was she really?

Beside the stone platform was a jade box. Chen Ji opened the lid, and inside lay a yellowed silk scroll. He carefully took it out and slowly unrolled it. When he saw the contents, his pupils constricted sharply—it was a list, recording dozens of names, and the very first name at the top of the list was precisely 'Liu Ruyan'.

dialogue.content: (The residual soul's voice carried a trace of remembrance) Liu Ruyan, one of the guardians selected by the Tianji Record ten thousand years ago. She was the source of the Chen bloodline, and also... your mother's original name.

text.content: The hand holding the silk scroll trembled slightly. A name from ten thousand years ago? The source of the Chen bloodline? He had always believed his mother was merely an ordinary mortal woman, living a simple life in seclusion after marrying his father. But now this testament letter told him she had never been ordinary from the start—she was a piece selected ten thousand years ago, woven into the critical nexus of the Tianji Record's web of fate.

choice.prompt: Faced with the truth of his mother's true identity, Chen Ji needed to make a choice—how should he confront this discovery that overturned everything he knew?

choices.description: Continue investigating deeply, not letting any clue slip, even if it may touch the forbidden realm of the Heavenly Eye.
choices.visible_reward: Uncover more connections between his mother and the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: The gaze of the Heavenly Eye may be watching all of this

text.content: Chen Ji carefully stored the silk scroll away, his gaze falling on an unremarkable hidden compartment beneath the stone platform. His fingers gently stroked the stone surface, sensing the residual spiritual energy within—very faint, but undeniably present. His mother's布局 was deeper than he had imagined.

choices.description: Deeply bury these discoveries in his heart, letting no one know, to prevent enemies from exploiting them.
choices.visible_reward: Guard the secret, accumulate strength in the shadows

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the silk scroll close to his body, his expression returning to its usual cold detachment. Whatever his mother might be, there was a reason she chose to leave. Before he had sufficient strength, he would not let anyone know about these things—not even the fragmented soul within the Tianji Record.

choices.description: Setting aside all calculations, simply feeling the traces his mother left behind, searching for the reason she chose to leave.
choices.visible_reward: Obtaining the Emotional Comfort Left by His Mother
choices.risk_hint: This may touch the softest place in his heart

text.content: Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, pressing the silk scroll against his chest. The fifteen years of coldness and calculation seemed to become less important in this moment. If his mother was truly someone chosen ten thousand years ago, then her departure... perhaps was never about abandoning him, but about protecting him.

Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded again, carrying a rare softness: "Liu Ruyan volunteered for reincarnation back then. She said only by diluting the bloodline to its faintest could she escape the tracking of the Heavenly Eye. And the Chen family... was her chosen continuation for herself." After a pause, the fragmented soul's voice grew deeper, "The blood flowing in you was carved with destiny ten thousand years ago."

Staring at the portrait, Chen Ji suddenly noticed a detail he had overlooked before—on the wrist of his mother in the painting hung a jade bracelet. The jade's quality and patterns were exactly like the broken jade fragment he had always treasured in his arms. That was something his mother had stuffed into his hands before leaving. He had always thought it was an ordinary ornament, never parted from it for fifteen years.

He took out that broken jade fragment. Just then, a faint tremor came from deep within the secret chamber. On the stone wall, a hidden door slid open silently, revealing a small space inside—only a simple stone table, on which lay a yellowed letter—no name on the envelope, just three characters: "吾儿启" (For My Son).

This was the first time in his memory that his mother had called him "吾儿" (my son). Before that, she always called him "Ji'er", her tone flat like she was calling a neighbor's child. He once thought she didn't love him enough, but now looking at these three characters, he noticed the handwriting trembled slightly, as if the writer was suppressing something.

choice.prompt: The letter his mother left was right before his eyes. Chen Ji was about to open this letter that had been sealed for fifteen years—his hands, were trembling slightly.

choices.description: Without hesitation, immediately open the letter to see what his mother left to say.
choices.visible_cost: May Not Be Able to Bear the Letter's Contents
choices.risk_hint: Reading the Letter in the Ruins May Expose One's Location

dialogue.content: (Reciting softly) "Ji'er, when you see this letter, Mother is no longer by your side. Do not resent Mother. Everything Mother did was to let you survive..."

choices.description: Carefully store the letter close to the body, and wait until returning to a safe place to study it carefully.
choices.visible_reward: Fully Experience Mother's Last Words in a Safe Environment
choices.risk_hint: The Letter May Be Lost While Waiting

text.content: Chen Ji placed the letter and silk scroll together against his chest, suppressing the urge to open them immediately. This was deep within the ruins, where danger could strike at any moment—the things his mother left, he would not allow any mishap.

The moment Chen Ji tucked the letter into his chest, a wave of warmth surged from his heart—the dormant jade fragment suddenly burst into soft white light. The radiance penetrated his clothing, casting a faint glow across the secret chamber. At the same time, he sensed his sister Chen Nian's direction, where the blood pulse resonance suddenly intensified more than tenfold.

Chen Ji's eyes reddened slightly. For fifteen years, he had woken countless times in the dead of night, curled up in cold blankets, thinking of the woman who said 'wait for me to return' yet never came back. He had hated her, hated her for abandoning her young self and sister. But now, gazing at the gentle smile of his mother in the portrait, something suddenly became clear to him.

She didn't abandon him—she protected him in her own way. A chess piece selected ten thousand years ago, reincarnated through cycles, just to pass the bloodline down to this generation—the Chen family's child was the endgame of her scheme spanning millennia. And what sacrifice lay behind her words 'to let you survive'?

The jade pendant glowing quietly in the ruins seemed to sense Chen Ji's presence, trembling slightly—as if calling out a name that had been lost for fifteen years. In the darkness beyond the secret chamber, an indistinct echo came from somewhere, the sound of fate's gears turning. Chen Ji gripped the jade fragment in his hand, his gaze gradually becoming resolute. No matter who his mother was, no matter what scheme she had laid—he would find her, find his sister, find the bloodline bond that fate had severed for fifteen years.
